input.quote: II. As compensation for the Licensee to use the Licensed Technology during the Initial Period, Licensee shall pay to Licensor, the following user fees:
input.rationale: The fee architecture (Art. V, ¶¶p0056–p0063 with p0066–p0070) is purely usage-based: Licensee pays a per-US$1 million traded rate set by the Monthly Notional Volume band actually reached, calculated and paid monthly in arrears. There is no committed volume, no minimum spend, no take-or-pay, no shortfall charge and no volume cap or floor imposed on Licensee's usage — searches for "minimum", "commit", "shortfall", "at least/not less than" and volume-cap language return nothing of that character. The tiered table is a discount schedule that benefits us at higher volumes, not a commitment. The only fixed recurring amount is the $2,500/month Technical Support Services fee (p0086), which is consideration for services actually delivered and so falls within the preferred position ("fees are for usage or ordered services only"). The p0070 floor ("In no event shall the amount payable ... be less than the amount recorded by the Licensee as being traded ... multiplied by the applicable Fees") is a floor measured by actual traded volume, not a minimum purchase obligation. Note for the wider review (outside this rule): the 36-month Initial Period with renewal solely at Licensor's option and no Licensee termination-for-convenience right is a term/exit issue for the TERM/TERMINATION rule, but because no take-or-pay or minimum volume is attached to that term, MINCOMMIT is satisfied and no redline is warranted here.
